edges.reason: _msgSender returns the untrusted msg.sender value.
onlyOwner gate on setExcludeFromBlackList resolves through _msgSender.
onlyOwner gate on setIncludeToBlackList resolves through _msgSender.
Constructor uses _msgSender to seed the deployer balance.
Constructor writes the full supply into _balances.
Constructor sets _owner to the deploy-time sender.
State initializer sets newComer to the deploy-time sender.
onlyOwner modifier compares newComer with _msgSender for setExcludeFromBlackList.
onlyOwner modifier compares newComer with _msgSender for setIncludeToBlackList.
setExcludeFromBlackList writes false into _includeToBlackList.
setIncludeToBlackList writes true into _includeToBlackList.
approve passes _msgSender as the allowance owner.
approve delegates to _approve.
transfer uses _msgSender as the sender of funds.
transfer calls _transfer.
transferFrom uses _msgSender as the spender for allowance checks.
transferFrom calls _transfer.
transferFrom calls _approve to decrement allowance.
_approve conditionally writes or zeroes _allowances.
_approve branches on owner() when deciding allowance behaviour.
owner() reads the _owner state variable.
_transfer reads and writes _balances for sender and recipient.
_transfer performs the balance subtraction via SafeMath.sub.
The subtraction result is written back into _balances.
allowance reads _allowances.
balanceOf reads _balances.
totalSupply reads _tTotal.
sender parameter drives the balance debit in _transfer.
recipient parameter drives the balance credit in _transfer.
amount parameter is the value moved by _transfer.
_account parameter is the key written by setExcludeFromBlackList.
_account parameter is the key written by setIncludeToBlackList.
ol parameter is the allowance owner key in _approve.
tt parameter is the spender key in _approve.
newOwner parameter is written into _owner by transferOwnership.
transferOwnership overwrites the _owner state variable.
renounceOwnership is guarded by onlyOwner via _msgSender.
renounceOwnership sets _owner to address(0).
Low-level value call forwards execution to a caller-supplied target, enabling reentrant control flow before state finalization.
The call recipient and the reentrant caller are both attacker-controlled addresses.
